name: Elevator
tagline: Small Python server that exposes multiple LevelDB databases over ZeroMQ and msgpack; idle since 2014.
description: Elevator was an open-source key-value server written in Python by Théo Crevon (oleiade) in 2012-2013. It wrapped several LevelDB databases behind one process, using plyvel for storage, and exposed them to remote clients over ZeroMQ sockets with msgpack-encoded messages, so a single LevelDB backend could be shared asynchronously by multithreaded or networked clients in any language with a ZeroMQ binding. It offered GET/PUT/DELETE, range and slice reads, batch writes and database management commands, plus a command-line client, Debian packages and a Puppet module. The PyPI package reached 0.5 in 2013 and the last commit was in May 2014. Projects wanting networked LevelDB-style storage today usually reach for Kvrocks, TiKV or plain RocksDB.
statusNote: No commits since May 2014; last PyPI release 0.5 (2013).
strengths: Turns embedded LevelDB into a shared network service with very little code
Ordered range reads and batch writes inherited from LevelDB
weaknesses: Unmaintained since 2014 and tied to Python 2-era dependencies and ZeroMQ 3
Python request handling caps throughput well below native servers
useCases: Learning how to wrap an embedded KV engine as a network server
